subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should reset archive recovery be solved through read-only family history only, a doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: The choice controls model/UI access to sensitive archived transcripts and whether OpenClaw mutates archived session files, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
options.body: Make the supported retrieval path an opt-in family/archive reader with bounded output, lineage checks, and clear source metadata before considering mutation recovery.

options.title: Add Doctor Restore/Re-Index
options.body: Provide a deliberate `openclaw doctor --fix` style recovery command for affected users that preserves archive provenance and warns about retention and privacy effects.

options.title: Reject Archive Mutation
options.body: Keep `.reset.*` archives immutable and route remaining recovery work to read-only history, export, and reset-policy improvements.

recommendation.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
recommendation.body: Make the supported retrieval path an opt-in family/archive reader with bounded output, lineage checks, and clear source metadata before considering mutation recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main routing candidate across the current schema/tool/history/fallback lines and the latest release snapshot.
